title: cudamempool fallback and pinned staging leak during KV-prefetch under continuous batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We are observing sustained growth in resident GPU memory and host pinned staging allocations on high-concurrency continuous-batching workloads that exercise KV cache prefetching. The growth correlates with cudaMemPool fallback paths and cudaHostRegister churn when batches arrive on low-priority streams. This ticket captures the investigation, reproducible test plan, experiments, hypotheses, and proposed mitigations.
problem_statement: On long-running serving nodes under continuous batching with aggressive KV cache prefetch/eviction, overall GPU resident memory and host pinned bytes increase steadily until eviction/oom conditions occur. The allocator (cudaMallocAsync + mempool) shows many short-lived allocations on different streams; we suspect fallback to default pool or synchronous pinned registration is leaving stale page-locked regions and holding device memory via delayed frees tied to stream ordering.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Run synthetic KV-prefetch load (script attached) that issues 2000 concurrent requests/sec with mixed seq lengths (16-4096) and prefetch=enabled.
2) Use continuous batching (batch max 64, max_wait 6ms) across three CUDA streams: main, prefetch-low-prio, background-io.
3) Monitor nvidia-smi, cuda memory pool metrics (via cuMemPoolGetAttribute where available), and host pinned bytes (smem/pss on pinned pages via driver traces).
4) Observe baseline at t=0 and measure growth over 4 hours.
Expected: steady-state plateau. Observed: linear growth in pinned host bytes and small but steady increase in GPU reserved/resident until eviction triggers throttling.
observations:
- Memory growth aligns with bursts of prefetch activity on low-priority streams.
- cudaMallocAsync backlog spikes on stream synchronization points (streamSynchronize in background cleanup).
- cuMemPool metrics indicate fallback to system allocator when per-pool exhausted; fallback paths call cuMemAlloc which appears to allocate separate arenas and triggers host pinned staging registrations during device-host transfers.
- Host pinned bytes (tracked via driver tracing) increase in tandem with fallback events.
- Kernel execution and batching throughput unaffected initially; tail latency increases as throttling begins.
- Leak not observed when prefetch is disabled or when all prefetch work is on the same stream as main inference stream.
hypotheses:
1) Per-stream mempool fragmentation: small allocations tied to prefetch create many short-lived arenas; when a mempool is exhausted, code falls back to cuMemAlloc (or cudaMallocAsync without pool), creating allocations that bypass pooling and perform implicit host pinning during staged transfers.
2) Stream priority ordering causes delayed release: frees are enqueued on a low-priority stream which never syncs promptly with the pool's eviction logic, leaving allocations resident until explicit synchronization.
3) Host pinned staging is performed redundantly for prefetch transfers when using fallback allocator; combined with delayed frees this results in pinned memory accumulation.
experiments_run:
- Experiment A (2026-01-12): Force single global mempool for all streams. Result: pinned growth reduced by ~70% but not eliminated; GPU resident growth slowed.
- Experiment B (2026-01-18): Pin all prefetch transfers to high-priority stream and add explicit cudaStreamSynchronize after prefetch completion. Result: pinned bytes plateaued; throughput dropped 4% due to synchronization overhead.
- Experiment C (2026-01-24): Patch runtime to disable mempool fallback and fail allocation instead of falling back. Result: immediate OOMs under peak load but confirmed fallback is correlated with pinned growth.
- Experiment D (2026-01-28): Replace host staging path to use registered persistent staging buffers (reused host pinned pages) instead of one-off cudaHostRegister in fallback path. Result: pinned bytes stable but added complexity and requires compatibility guard for older drivers.

decision_notes:
Short-term mitigation: throttle KV prefetch concurrency and prefer reuse of a shared mempool across streams. Implement a runtime guard that disables fallback to unpooled allocations unless under explicit customer opt-in.
Long-term options:
- Improve per-pool sizing heuristics and introduce cross-stream compaction/defragmentation.
- Implement a persistent host-pinned staging allocator to avoid repeated cudaHostRegister calls.
- Instrument mempool fallback paths to emit high-cardinality metrics and alerts for early detection.
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Disabling fallback reduces robustness under unexpected allocation spikes; may cause user-visible OOMs for some workloads (tradeoff between predictable memory usage vs availability).
- Introducing synchronous stream sync for prefetch stabilizes memory but adds latency risk.
- Persistent host-pinned staging reduces CPU memory churn but increases complexity and compatibility surface with older CUDA drivers.
next_steps:
1) Ship conservative runtime change (runtime-1.22 patch) that: a) uses a shared mempool for prefetch streams by default, b) emits metrics when fallback happens, and c) limits per-request prefetch concurrency to 8. Target eta 2026-02-05.
2) Add E2E test in CI that runs repro for 30 minutes to detect pinned growth regressions.
3) Design persistent staging allocator RFC (assigned to Marco) due 2026-02-12.
4) Run customer canary with small subset of Dedicated nodes and monitor dashboards for 48 hours.
